answer_sentences.text: No, for an individual retail borrower taking a non-business loan, the penal charges cannot be higher than those applied to a non-individual borrower for the same kind of non-compliance.
answer_sentences.quote: The penal charges in case of loans sanctioned to ‘individual borrowers, for purposes other than business’, shall not be higher than the penal charges applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance of material terms and conditions.

answer_sentences.text: The RBI directions also require that any default penalty be levied only as penal charges, not as penal interest, and that those charges be reasonable and non-discriminatory.
answer_sentences.quote: penalty, if charged, for such default shall only be levied in the form of penal charges and not penal interest. Such penal charges shall be reasonable and levied by the lenders only on the amount under default in a non-discriminatory manner as per their Board approved policy.
